verses.text: When Jesus finished saying all this, he told his disciples,
“You know Passover is two days away. The Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”
Then the chief priests, teachers of the Law, and elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest Caiaphas.
They plotted to arrest Jesus by trickery and kill him.
But they said, “Not during the festival, or the people might riot.”
Jesus was in Bethany at the home of Simon, who had leprosy.
A woman came over with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfume. While Jesus was eating, she poured it on his head.
When the disciples saw it, they were upset: “Why waste it like this?”
“This perfume could’ve been sold for a lot and the money given to the poor.”
Jesus knew what they were saying and told them, “Why are you giving this woman a hard time? She’s done something good for me.”
“You’ll always have the poor with you, but you won’t always have me.”
“By pouring this perfume on my body, she was getting me ready for burial.”
“I’m telling you the truth: wherever this Good News is announced throughout the world, people will tell what she did in memory of her.”
Then one of the twelve, Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and asked, “What will you give me if I hand him over to you?” They counted out thirty silver coins for him.
From then on, Judas looked for the right chance to betray Jesus.
On the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the disciples asked Jesus, “Where do you want us to prepare the Passover meal for you?”
He said, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is near. I’ll celebrate Passover at your house with my disciples.”’”
The disciples did what Jesus told them and prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, Jesus was reclining at the table with the twelve.
As they ate, he said, “I’m telling you the truth: one of you will betray me.”
They were deeply upset, and each one began asking him, “Surely it isn’t me, Lord?”
He answered, “The one who dipped his hand in the dish with me is the one who’ll betray me.”
“The Son of Man will go as Scripture says, but how terrible for the one who betrays him! It would’ve been better for that person never to be born.”
Judas, who was about to betray him, asked, “Surely it isn’t me, Rabbi?” Jesus answered, “You said it.”
As they ate, Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and handed it to the disciples. “Take this and eat it. This is my body.”
He took a cup, gave thanks, and passed it to them: “All of you drink from it.”
“This is my blood of the new covenant, poured out for many so their sins can be forgiven.”
“I’m telling you, I won’t drink this fruit of the vine again until that day I drink it new with you in my Father’s Kingdom.”
After they sang a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus told them, “Tonight you’ll all stumble because of me. Scripture says, ‘I’ll strike the shepherd, and the flock’s sheep will scatter.’”
“But after I’m raised, I’ll go ahead of you into Galilee.”
Peter answered, “Even if everyone else stumbles because of you, I never will.”
Jesus told him, “I’m telling you the truth: before the rooster crows tonight, you’ll deny me three times.”
Peter said, “Even if I have to die with you, I won’t deny you.” All the other disciples said the same.
Then Jesus went with them to a place called Gethsemane. He told the disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
He took Peter and Zebedee’s two sons with him. Grief and deep distress came over him.
Jesus told them, “My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow, even to death. Stay here and keep watch with me.”
He went a little farther, fell facedown, and prayed: “My Father, if there’s any way, let this cup pass from me. But not what I want—what you want.”
He came back to the disciples and found them asleep. He said to Peter, “Couldn’t you stay awake with me for one hour?”
“Stay awake and pray so you don’t give in to temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
Again he went away and prayed: “My Father, if this cup can’t pass unless I drink it, let your will be done.”
He came back and found them asleep again. Their eyes were heavy.
He left them again, went away, and prayed a third time, saying the same thing.
Then he came back to the disciples and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour is near. The Son of Man is being handed over to sinners.”
“Get up, let’s go. The one betraying me is close.”
While he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived with a huge crowd carrying swords and clubs. They’d been sent by the chief priests and elders.
The betrayer had given them a signal: “The man I kiss is the one. Grab him.”
Right away Judas came up to Jesus: “Greetings, Rabbi!” He kissed him.
Jesus said to him, “Friend, what did you come for?” Then they came up, grabbed Jesus, and arrested him.
One of the people with Jesus reached for his sword. He struck the high priest’s servant and cut off his ear.
Jesus told him, “Put your sword away. Everyone who takes up the sword will die by the sword.”
“Do you think I can’t ask my Father for help? He could send me more than twelve legions of angels right now.”
“But then how would Scripture be fulfilled? It has to happen this way.”
At that moment Jesus said to the crowd, “Did you come after me with swords and clubs like I’m a robber? I sat in the temple teaching every day, and you didn’t arrest me.”
“But all this happened to fulfill what the prophets wrote.” Then all the disciples left him and ran away.
The people who arrested Jesus took him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the teachers of the Law and elders had gathered.
Peter followed from a distance to the high priest’s courtyard. He went in and sat with the officers to see how it would end.
The chief priests, elders, and whole council looked for false testimony against Jesus so they could put him to death.
Many false witnesses came forward, but they found nothing. Finally, two false witnesses came up
and said, “This man claimed, ‘I can destroy God’s temple and rebuild it in three days.’”
The high priest stood up and asked Jesus, “Aren’t you going to answer? What do you say to these accusations?”
But Jesus stayed silent. The high priest said, “I command you by the living God: tell us if you are the Christ, God’s Son.”
Jesus answered, “You’ve said it. But I’m telling you, from now on you’ll see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on heaven’s clouds.”
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, “He has spoken blasphemy! Why do we need more witnesses? You heard it yourselves.”
“What’s your verdict?” They answered, “He deserves death!”
Then they spat in his face and punched him. Others slapped him,
saying, “Prophesy for us, Christ! Who hit you?”
Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard when a servant girl came up and said, “You were with Jesus from Galilee too!”
But he denied it in front of everyone: “I don’t know what you’re talking about.”
He went out to the porch. Another person saw him and told the people there, “This man was with Jesus from Nazareth.”
Again Peter denied it, swearing an oath: “I don’t know the man.”
A little later, the people standing there came up to Peter: “You’re definitely one of them. Your accent gives you away.”
Then he started cursing and swearing: “I don’t know the man!” Right then, a rooster crowed.
Peter remembered what Jesus had said: “Before the rooster crows, you’ll deny me three times.” He went outside and wept bitterly.
